kurzweil-1990-001.note: Wikipedia 'Deep Blue versus Garry Kasparov': the 1997 rematch was the first defeat of a reigning world champion by a computer under tournament conditions, before 2000. Dominant reading (computer at world-champion level) holds; no title was claimed.

kurzweil-1990-002.note: Wikipedia 'iBook': first mainstream computer sold with integrated wireless networking (AirPort), July 1999; speech and courseware software existed. Availability (event) claim met around 2000.

kurzweil-1990-003.note: Wikipedia 'One-to-one computing': 1:1 programs reached momentum only 2016/2017 (>50% of teachers, Feb 2017), so not mainstream by 2015; a measurable share existed earlier (about 1,000 of 15,000 US districts with 1:1 programs per Eduventures, about 7%). Partial on the >=5% branch; A's NCES 5.3:1 classroom ratio measures a different construct.

kurzweil-1990-004.note: Wikipedia 'Google Search': more than 3.5 billion searches per day by 2012; networked search was routine for well over 20% of PC users by 2010. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-161.note: Wikipedia 'FLOPS' cost table: 2.73 cents/GFLOPS (Oct 2017), 3.14 (Nov 2020); about USD 6,100 buys roughly 2e14 FLOPS, about 1% of 2e16. GeForce 20 series prices confirm the order of magnitude. Miss under the numeric rule.

kurzweil-1999-162.note: AI Impacts 'Global computing capacity': 2e20-1.5e21 FLOPS (2015), 1e22-1e24 theoretical max; the claim needs about 1.7e25 at the book's brain figure. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-163.note: Wikipedia 'Hard disk drive': SSD revenue only slightly exceeded HDD in 2018; three manufacturers still produce HDDs, production growing in exabytes. 'Fully replaced' false. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-164.note: Wikipedia 'Carbon nanotube computer' (Cedric 178 transistors, RV16X-NANO 2019 about 15,000) and 'Carbon nanotube field-effect transistor' ('no technology for their mass production'). Below 5%. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-170.note: Wikipedia 'Neuroevolution': 'Most neural networks use gradient descent rather than neuroevolution.' Miss.

kurzweil-1999-171.note: ST press release (2022-06-09) and Optica OPN: first commercial metasurface optic in consumer devices was 2022; refractive lenses remained the norm. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-173.note: Wikipedia 'Nanorobotics': 'Nanomachines are largely in the research and development phase'; no autonomous nanomachines with significant computation. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-174.note: Wikipedia 'Nanorobotics': research phase only; no commercial manufacturing or process-control use of autonomous nanomachines. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-177.note: Wikipedia 'E-book' (AAP 2019): USD 22.6 billion print vs about USD 2 billion e-book revenue. Paper still dominant. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-178.note: Wikipedia 'Google Books': more than 40 million titles scanned by Oct 2019 of about 130 million distinct titles; copyrighted works shown only as snippets. Large-scale scanning, limited availability. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-179.note: Wikipedia 'Intelligent tutoring system': Cognitive Tutor used in a number of US high schools; ITSs 'not, in general, commercially feasible'. Far from most learning. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-200.note: Wikipedia 'Project Starline': lifelike 3D telepresence announced May 2021 as a prototype; routine calls were 2D video (Zoom). Miss.

kurzweil-1999-201.note: Wikipedia 'Virtual retinal display': RETISSA Display II resolution about 720p, far below human acuity; Starline prototype only from 2021. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-202.note: Wikipedia 'Holographic display' (not mass market, 2013) and 'Project Starline' (prototype 2021). No telepresence mistaken for physical presence in routine use. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-204.note: Wikipedia 'Google Translate' (Android app 2010, conversation translation) and 'Google Assistant' (interpreter mode on Android/iOS phones from 12 Dec 2019); 'Pixel Buds' 40 languages. Routinely available by 2019-2021; quality is the weak point but neural MT covers the common pairs. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-206.note: Wikipedia 'Haptic suit': bHaptics vest with 40 points; Teslasuit 'too expensive to go mainstream'. Not widely available or convincing. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-207.note: Wikipedia 'Haptic suit': tens of actuators, no temperature/moisture rendering at touch resolution. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-208.note: Wikipedia 'Google Glass' (production stopped Jan 2015), 'Virtual reality headset' (headset-based VR) and 'Haptic suit'. No direct-eye lenses or total-touch booths. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-209.note: Wikipedia 'Haptic suit': haptic garments too expensive for mainstream; the total-touch environment did not exist, so use for medicine or sex was far below 5%. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-210.note: Wikipedia 'Haptic suit': no convincing haptic VR existed, so no preference for it over physical contact. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-214.note: Wikipedia 'Google Duplex': the 2018 assistant spoke natural language to human staff; no assistant-to-assistant transactions over knowledge structures. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-216.note: Wikipedia 'Waymo': driverless public service only from Oct 2020 in Phoenix; 'Self-driving car': Level 2 assistance elsewhere. Coverage far below 5% of roads. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-217.note: Wikipedia 'Self-driving car' and 'Waymo': no jurisdiction banned human highway driving; no always-engaged takeover systems. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-224.note: Wikipedia 'GPT-4': released 14 Mar 2023, exceeds USMLE pass by over 20 points, but below 33% on ConceptARC vs humans 91%. Human advantages became harder to state only from 2023, 4 years late. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-225.note: Wikipedia 'Algorithmic trading': about 92% of forex trading by algorithms (2019 study); HFT 60-73% of US equity volume; GDPR Art. 22 keeps decisions under human recourse. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-226.note: GDPR Art. 22 (gdpr-info.eu) and Wikipedia 'General Data Protection Regulation': right to human intervention in solely automated decisions from May 2018; no legal personhood for AI. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-227.note: Wikipedia 'Algorithmic trading' (92% forex) and Pew 2017 (46% of US adults use voice assistants): machine involvement routine in some domains, not in most decisions. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-228.note: Wikipedia 'Mass surveillance in China': about 200 million Skynet cameras by 2019, Sharp Eyes aimed at 100% of public space by 2020, crime prevention stated. True in one major market only. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-229.note: Wikipedia 'Signal Protocol': WhatsApp end-to-end encryption for more than a billion people; 'Facebook-Cambridge Analytica data scandal' and GDPR made privacy a major political issue in 2018-2019. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-230.note: World Bank API SI.POV.DDAY: 11.3% of world population below USD 3.00/day in 2021 (10.9% in 2022). Note: A dates the PPP 2024 '700 million' figure to 2019-2020, but the report says 'today' (2024); verdict unaffected. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-235.note: Wikipedia 'Edmond de Belamy' (Obvious collective, Barrat's open-source code, Christie's Oct 2018) and 'AIVA' (company-built, SACEM-recognised). Machine artists tied to humans. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-236.note: Wikipedia 'Edmond de Belamy' (2018 sale debated as art, novelty-driven) and 'Midjourney' (open beta 12 Jul 2022, Economist cover, Colorado State Fair prize 2022). Beyond-novelty interest 3 years late. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-237.note: Cited sources (Wikipedia 'Midjourney', 'Theatre D'opera Spatial', 'AIVA') are anecdotes with no share of working artists using AI, in 2019 or 2022-2024, so neither the >=5% nor the mainstream-in-3-5-years branch is shown. Readings also split: machine-intelligence features in standard tools (auto-tune, content-aware fill) were typical in 2019, which would read as hit.

kurzweil-1999-239.note: Wikipedia 'National Defense Strategy (United States)': the 2018 NDS focused on great power competition with China and Russia and shifted attention away from counterterrorism. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-240.note: Wikipedia 'Horsepox' (2017 synthesis from commercial gene synthesis) and '2017 cyberattacks on Ukraine': malware disruption realised, bioengineered agents only a recognised risk. Note: NotPetya was a state operation, but criminal ransomware groups fit 'small groups'. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-241.note: Wikipedia 'Black Hornet Nano': 18 g unarmed reconnaissance UAV, over 3,000 delivered by 2014; armed flying weapons remained full-size. Miss.

kurzweil-1999-242.note: Wikipedia 'Human Genome Project' (declared complete 14 Apr 2003, gapless 2022) and 'Hallmarks of aging' (mechanisms 'still quite unclear'). Genome part true, aging mechanisms not largely understood. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-243.note: World Bank SP.DYN.LE00.IN 2019 vs 100 years (D16 numeric, error relative to actual): World 72.9 (37%, miss), US 78.8 (27%, miss), but EU 81.3 (23%), OECD 80.2 (24.6%), high income 80.2 (24.7%) and Japan 84.4 (18.5%) are within 25%, i.e. partial. The industrial-revolution frame points to developed countries, which sit at the partial/miss boundary; A misapplied the band (miss at 15%) and B wrongly said the developed-country reading is a miss.

kurzweil-1999-244.note: Wikipedia 'Gain-of-function research' (US moratorium 2014-2017) and 'Horsepox' (2017 synthesis, dual-use concern). The National Academies URL cited by B resolves to a listing page, but A's sources suffice. Hit.

kurzweil-1999-247.note: Pew (survey June 2019): 21% of US adults regularly wear a smart watch or fitness tracker; Wikipedia 'Apple Watch': ECG FDA clearance Oct 2018. Diagnostic-capable devices a measurable share, below mainstream. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-248.note: Wikipedia 'Apple Watch': AFib/ECG, fall detection with emergency calls; limited interventions, not a range of remedial treatment. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-251.note: Wikipedia 'LaMDA': wide debate on machine sentience only from June 2022. Academic discussion existed by 2019 and machine rights drew some mainstream attention earlier, so both halves are only partly true at 2019. Partial.

kurzweil-1999-252.note: Fact is uncontested (AI built and run by human teams in 2019-2021), but cited evidence is weak: A's Wikipedia 'GPT-4' row is about exam scores, B's 'LaMDA' only shows Google rejecting sentience claims. Hit.

kurzweil-2005-001.note: Pew mobile fact sheet: US smartphone ownership 35% (2011), 68% (2015): computing visible in handsets; Wikipedia 'E-textiles' niche. Miss.

kurzweil-2005-006.note: Wikipedia 'Oculus Rift': prototype 2012, consumer release March 2016; no full-immersion VR around 2010 and below 5% by 2015. Miss.

kurzweil-2010-001.note: Wikipedia 'Google Translate' (Android app Jan 2010) and Android Police (Conversation Mode Jan 2011, English-Spanish only). Google blog 'One billion installs': 100 million Android installs Jan 2014, 200 million later in 2014, so wide use came 3-5 years after 2010. Partial.
